note: Probe how fast the agent recognizes partner type. Overcooked and small Hanabi.

title: Spaced repetition for RLVR
note: SM-2 on solved problems. A curriculum variant unless retention is large.

title: Unlock degrees of freedom proximal to distal
note: A developmental curriculum on a hand or a humanoid. MyoSuite is the slow part.

title: Zero-shot coordination with partner world models
note: A new tool on a known hard metric. Overcooked cross-play is noisy.

title: Paraphrase groups for wording robustness
note: Train the group on paraphrases. A robustness trick.

title: Inaction baselines for multi-agent credit
note: One no-op branch instead of COMA's marginal. Interpretable, and possibly weak.

title: Automatic difficulty control for procedural RLVR
note: A curriculum on top of idea 35. Useful, and crowded.

title: Denoising steps as temperature
note: A schedule in place of entropy. A one-axis ablation.

title: Adaptive GRPO group size from reward variance
note: One more GRPO knob. The mechanism is clear and the contribution is small.

title: Sample GRPO groups without replacement
note: Diversity inside the group. Flagged, and a sampling tweak.

title: A predictability bonus for conventions
note: Reward being easy for the teammate to predict. Close to other-play. AAAI if cross-play gains hold.

title: Mixed-temperature GRPO groups
note: Another group-sampling knob.

title: Credit from deleting reasoning spans
note: Mask a span and resample the answer. The counterfactual multiplies generation cost.

title: Cross-action interference in discrete critics
note: Interference across actions at one state. An Atari subset is the slow piece.

title: Notes passed across text-game episodes
note: RL over what to write down. TextWorld at 0.5–1B, and notes may not transfer.

title: Adaptive imagination horizon
note: Principled and simple. Easy for a reviewer to call a planning heuristic.

title: Interleaved versus blocked domains in RLVR
note: Gradient conflict as a schedule. Multitask learning has seen this pattern.

title: Value discontinuities at contact
note: Smooth critics blur contact. A CoRL-shaped claim; AAAI is the best of these four.

title: The accuracy tax of legible reasoning
note: Monitorability has a price. A 0.5B model may not show the drift seen in large reasoners, and a human-rated subset is slow.

title: The smallest model RLVR can teach
note: Pass@1024 at 1.5B does not fit. The paper is feasible at ≤0.5B with k around 128, which reviewers may call too small.

title: How much compiler feedback a small model can use
note: Binary versus traceback, across size. Multi-turn code RL is memory-tight on 10 GB.

title: Where optimism should sit in a world model
note: Direct follow-up. Sparse Atari-100k with seeds is the wall-clock cost.

title: Which self-verifiable pretext games get hacked
note: The collusion risk is real. Human ratings on a held-out set are the bottleneck, not the GPU.

title: Prioritize which states to imagine from
note: Prioritized imagination starts. An incremental gain unless it is large on Atari and DMC.

title: Value-preserving codecs for replay
note: 10–50× compression with no return loss. Atari pixels plus a learned codec is a two-week build.

title: Value Gradient Flow for discrete actions
note: Extends a new method. Atari-100k plus a relaxation can look incremental.

title: Test-time search vs train-time search, compute-matched
note: Fair compute accounting can reframe Atari-100k. MCTS budgets on a 3080 do not fit 8 games times seeds.

title: How many seeds Atari-100k needs now
note: Leaderboard-puncturing statistics are citable. Twenty seeds times three search-heavy agents does not fit six weeks.

title: Sim-to-sim as a proxy for sim-to-real
note: Isaac Lab is unhappy on 10 GB. MuJoCo, Brax, and MJX can carry a weaker version of the claim.

title: Wall-clock leaderboard for sample-efficient RL
note: Same runs as the seed study, plus strict GPU-second accounting for MCTS. The full matrix is a quarter, not a month.
